title: Exploration At Its Finest (unexpected shipwreck discovery, May 16, 2019)
place: Gulf of Mexico seafloor (Okeanos Explorer Shakedown and Sea Trials 2019, EX1902; ROV Deep Discoverer)
audio: track present in source (probably music); mute it
notes: Civilian wreck: a likely mid-19th-century wooden sailing vessel, NOT military. 0-5.6 s: the ghostly bow of the wooden hull looms out of the dark under the ROV's pinkish light, with ROV frame parts silhouetted in the left and bottom-right corners (x<0.2 and x>0.8; mostly removed by a square crop). Static shot. Bow subject at x~0.55. 5.6-12 s: a clean, static, well-lit view of the bow and stem rising from the sand, with the planked hull sweeping right. Subject (stem) at x~0.4, hull extends to x~0.9. Best seconds 5.6-12 (the creepiest and cleanest). The cut is 12 s, not 14, because the shot before is a dim ROV view and the next shot is hazy with ROV hardware in the frame. Native 1920x1080 at 29.97 fps, resampled to 30. No people, no logos or text in the window (the NOAA title card is at 0-4 s of the source; the end card and URL are at 2:31+).
fact_en: Experts suspect the wreck is that of a sailing vessel built sometime in the mid-19th century, perhaps a schooner or brig, measuring roughly 37.8 meters (124 feet) long; it was discovered unexpectedly on May 16, 2019 during an 'engineering dive' to test new ROV equipment.
